entries.name: Paul Salstrom

expected_cases.charges: Conscientious resistance to military conscription; individual statutory count unverified
expected_cases.sentence: Salstrom dates his arrival at the Medical Center for Federal Prisoners near Springfield, Missouri, to 1962 and describes two years incarcerated there. Contemporary October and November 1964 reports establish that he completed this term and was then arrested again in October 1964. The later Danbury custody is a separate episode. Exact admission and release days for the initial term remain unverified.

updates.charges: Alleged violation of release conditions through work in the peace movement
updates.sentence: Re-arrested in early October 1964 after completing his earlier Springfield term. Contemporary reporting attributes the arrest to peace-movement work in violation of release conditions. Later prisoner rosters place him at Danbury. The imposed term, exact custody admission and release dates, and time served in this separate episode remain unverified.

entries.rationale: Contemporary October and November1964 articles explicitly distinguish rearrest from completed initial term. Preserve initial24months; no duplicate numeric custody duration for later Danbury stay.

entries.name: James Groppi

expected_cases.charges: Contempt of the Wisconsin State Assembly following the September 29, 1969 welfare-rights demonstration in the Assembly chamber.
expected_cases.convicted: Contempt finding; overturned by the U.S. Supreme Court in Groppi v. Leslie, 404 U.S. 496 (1972).
expected_cases.sentence: Six months or the remainder of the legislative session, whichever was shorter. Actually served 10 days before federal release on bail; the contempt action was subsequently overturned.

updates.charges: Probation revocation on a resisting-an-officer conviction arising from the August 31, 1967 Milwaukee open-housing protest
updates.convicted: Convicted in 1968; the U.S. Supreme Court vacated the appellate judgment and remanded on January 25, 1971 (Groppi v. Wisconsin, 400 U.S. 505).
updates.sentence: Six-month sentence activated on October 17, 1969, with six days of custody credit after re-arrest on October 11. Justice Thurgood Marshall stayed execution and ordered release on October 27 pending review. The actual release date remains unverified. This episode is separate from the October 1–11 legislative-contempt confinement.

entries.rationale: LDF appellate brief printedp3 footnote2, retrieved indexed original OCR, explicitly dates October11rearrest and October17activation with sixdays credit. Contemporary AP corroborates activation and October27release order. Release order is not proof actual discharge; no release endpoint or full duration inferred. October17 field records activation, not original1968suspended sentence. SupremeCourt outcome separately verified.
